_readme: THE THROW-BACK PROTOCOL (Baseline System v1, section 6).
Code never draws, traces, generates or sources art, icons, photos,
logos, record art, letter variants or scribbles, and never writes copy
or quotes. When a component needs one it gets an entry here and the
An entry that is not `approved` renders NOTHING in production. In dev
(?dev=1 or localhost) it renders a labelled grey tile so the slot is
visible while building. `npm run audit` prints N slots unfilled.
path is filled in when the file lands, relative to the repo root.
ASSET_REQUESTS.md carries the longer prose version of the P1 list;
this file is what the build and the audit read.

requests.purpose: Hero name lockup, and case numbers on work rows. Three cuts of every letter so the comic boil has something to swap between; with one cut the preset does nothing by design rather than faking a wobble. RECEIVED 30 Oct as a sheet (assets/img/alphabet.webp) and sliced into 67 transparent cuts. Still short: Q is not on the sheet, and V, W, X and Z have one cut each, so the comic boil cannot swap those four.
requests.size: each letter ~800px on its longest edge
requests.format: PNG or WebP with real alpha, one file per letter per variant
requests.style-rule: his own alphabet sheet, cut from found print. No tracing, no generated letterforms, no font standing in for a cut-out.

requests.purpose: A taped cut-out thumbnail per case, five in total. The posters already on the site are his designed covers, which is a different artefact.
requests.style-rule: his own screenshots, taped and cut by hand. Not a crop of the poster.

requests.purpose: The hand-circled proof number on each work row.
requests.style-rule: his scanned circle mark. A drawn circle is his hand or it is not the device.

requests.purpose: Stitched postcard with a stamp and a Melbourne postmark, behind the contact actions.
requests.style-rule: his artwork. Nothing on the site is a postcard yet; this would be the first.

requests.purpose: One hand-drawn arrow pointing at the email button.
requests.style-rule: his hand, same rule as the proof circle.

requests.purpose: The colour original of the 2003 Delhi frame. The brush device reveals colour into the black-and-white print; today it keys off the same halftone, so what it reveals is a saturated version rather than true colour.
Names and roles for the six colleague quotes. The component refuses to render an unattributed quote, so the strip is absent until these land.
requests.format: text, one line per quote: name, role, company
requests.style-rule: his colleagues' real names, with their permission. Code does not write quotes or invent attributions.

requests.purpose: The resume as a PDF. The only file on disk is a .docx and labelling a Word file as a PDF is the kind of small lie this portfolio cannot afford, so the row currently says Word document.

One line per verified figure answering how it was measured: instrument, window, baseline. Fourteen of them. A tile with no method renders no reveal at all - an empty tooltip reads as a broken tooltip.
requests.style-rule: only he knows these. Code does not invent a measurement.

requests.purpose: The window each figure covers. An empty period renders no element at all; never TBC.
